papers.title: Practical Error Suppression and Mitigation for Reliable Quantum Computing
papers.abstract: Quantum computing is entering a transitional regime between noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) processing and early fault-tolerant quantum computation (FTQC), in which increasingly capable hardware is beginning to support repeated syndrome measurements, partial error correction, and logical-qubit operations, while residual physical and logical errors remain non-negligible. In this regime, error suppression, error mitigation, and quantum error correction are increasingly better viewed as complementary layers of a unified error-reduction strategy rather than as separate approaches, with each acting at a different stage of the quantum computation to improve simulation reliability. Thus, in this review, we provide a practical and forward-looking overview of the principal hardware error sources and the corresponding error suppression and mitigation methods for reducing their impact across the current NISQ-FTQC transition. We discuss hardware-aware circuit design, coherent-error suppression, readout mitigation, noise extrapolation, classical inference, and software-supported workflows, with particular emphasis on their implementation on actual quantum processors. We further examine how error mitigation techniques can be adapted to encoded and logical-qubit settings so that they can operate alongside quantum error correction to suppress residual logical errors and improve the accuracy of computation in the early fault-tolerant regime.

summary.summary: This review surveys error suppression and mitigation techniques across the NISQ-to-FTQC transition, treating error correction, suppression, and mitigation as complementary layers of a unified strategy rather than isolated approaches. The work emphasizes practical implementation of hardware-aware circuit design, coherent-error suppression, readout mitigation, noise extrapolation, and classical inference on near-term devices, with extensions to encoded and logical-qubit settings.
summary.motivation: Near-term quantum processors operate in a regime where physical and logical errors remain substantial despite growing capabilities for syndrome measurement and partial error correction, necessitating integrated error-reduction strategies that combine multiple techniques at different computational stages.
summary.method: The authors provide a comprehensive practical overview of principal hardware error sources and corresponding suppression/mitigation methods, covering hardware-aware design, coherent-error suppression techniques, readout error mitigation, noise extrapolation schemes, classical inference approaches, and software workflows with emphasis on actual processor implementations, plus adaptation of mitigation to encoded/logical-qubit regimes.
summary.result: The review synthesizes how error suppression, mitigation, and quantum error correction function as complementary layers to reduce both physical and logical errors, enabling improved simulation reliability and computational accuracy across the current NISQ-FTQC transition.
